claims.explanation: Metoprolol is a beta-adrenergic receptor antagonist whose anticancer selectivity likely reflects dependence on ADRB2-mediated cAMP/PKA signaling, which is known to promote survival and proliferation in melanoma and other neural-crest-derived tumors. Lines with high ADRB2 expression or BRAF/NRAS-driven MAPK activation (melanomas, some gastric and kidney lines) appear most sensitive, while lines with low adrenergic tone or alternative survival pathways are protected. The virtual-cell upregulation of ADRB2 and similarity to adrenergic ligands supports an on-target adrenergic mechanism rather than a general cytotoxic effect.

features.basis: on-target beta-2 adrenergic receptor mediating cAMP/PKA survival signaling; virtual cell shows ADRB2 upregulation
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are enriched among most-killed lines, consistent with MAPK-driven adrenergic crosstalk
NRAS-mutant melanoma and bladder lines appear in sensitive group, suggesting MAPK dependence
annotated metoprolol target; beta-1 signaling can support tumor cell survival
TP53 mutation is common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is not selective; listed as weak negative
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) are mostly in least-affected group
KRAS-mutant pancreatic, ovarian, and gastric lines are enriched among least-affected lines
PTEN loss appears in several sensitive lines (UACC62, 786O, HEC265), possibly via PI3K/AKT dependence
metoprolol is a CYP2D6 substrate; high CYP2D6 expression could reduce active drug exposure
PIK3CA mutations appear in several sensitive lines (HGC27, KYSE510, SNUC5, KE39)
CDKN2A loss is common in sensitive melanoma lines (K029AX, IPC298, MHHES1)
NF1 mutations appear in several least-affected lines (LOXIMVI is sensitive but many resistant lines carry NF1)
